```conf
# ~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf — Linux app-* helper overrides
#
# Sourced by ~/.config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh at shell startup (if present).
# NOT auto-stubbed by chezmoi — hand-maintained, mirrors the .shellrc.secrets
# convention. NOT tracked by git (lives under ~/.config/shell/ but chezmoi
# only manages files it knows about; this one stays personal).
#
# Each linux_app_register call:
#   --desktop=ID       .desktop stem (resolves applaunch via gtk-launch)
#   --exec=PATH        explicit launch command (apps with NO .desktop)
#   --pkill=REGEX      pgrep/pkill -f pattern (resolves appquit/apprunning)
#   --wm-class=CLASS   WM_CLASS for window-calls extension (true focus)
#   --mpris=NAME       playerctl -p name (resolves appresponsive)
#
# `linux_app_register --list` to print the current registry.
# `linux_app_register --help` for full flag reference.
# `pitfalls/linux-app-control-appimage-runtime-path.md` for AppImage gotchas.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Apt-installed Electron apps — Exec path matches runtime 1:1
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Cursor — apt at /usr/share/cursor/cursor. Also has a stale AppImage residue
# at ~/Applications/cursor.AppImage; --pkill anchors to /usr/share so we
# never accidentally target the unused AppImage path.
linux_app_register Cursor \
  --desktop=cursor \
  --pkill='^/usr/share/cursor/cursor( |$)' \
  --wm-class=Cursor

# Discord — apt at /usr/bin/discord -> /usr/share/discord/Discord. Flatpak
# com.discordapp.Discord is also installed but not running; --pkill targets
# the apt path so we don't quit the wrong copy.
linux_app_register Discord \
  --desktop=discord \
  --pkill='^/usr/share/discord/Discord( |$)' \
  --wm-class=discord

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Snap — wrapper at /snap/bin/<name>, runtime at /snap/<name>/<rev>/...
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Spotify — snap-confined. [^/]+ in --pkill matches any revision number so
# the pattern survives `snap refresh`. --mpris unlocks appresponsive.
linux_app_register Spotify \
  --desktop=spotify_spotify \
  --pkill='^/snap/spotify/[^/]+/usr/share/spotify/spotify' \
  --wm-class=spotify \
  --mpris=spotify

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AppImage — runtime path != .desktop Exec (FUSE mount at /tmp/.mount_*/)
# See pitfalls/linux-app-control-appimage-runtime-path.md
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Zen Browser — AppImage. Inner binary is `zen` (Firefox-fork). The user has
# 4 .desktop entries for Zen (cruft); --desktop pins the canonical one.
# Pattern matches the FUSE-mounted inner binary, not the .AppImage path.
linux_app_register Zen \
  --desktop=zen-browser \
  --pkill='\.mount_.+/zen($| )' \
  --wm-class=zen

# Frpc-Desktop — AppImage at ~/Applications/Frpc-Desktop-<version>.AppImage.
# The .desktop hash will change if the user re-downloads via AppImageLauncher;
# update --desktop= when that happens (find via:
#   ls ~/.local/share/applications/appimagekit_*Frpc*.desktop ).
linux_app_register Frpc-Desktop \
  --desktop=appimagekit_557220393761292184db845cd26816c3-Frpc-Desktop \
  --pkill='\.mount_.+/frpc-desktop($| )' \
  --wm-class=Frpc-Desktop

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Manually-placed (no .desktop) — use --exec= for the launch path
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Clash for Windows — Electron app, manually placed at
# ~/Documents/ClashForWindows/cfw. NO .desktop file → applaunch via --exec=
# (helper expands ~ and execs via `setsid -f sh -c`).
# CFW spawns a sidecar `clash-linux` at .../resources/static/files/linux/x64/
# and a service at ~/.config/clash/service/clash-core-service — those are NOT
# matched by --pkill (intentional — they survive appquit so the proxy stays
# up while the UI restarts; if you want them gone too, broaden the regex to
# 'ClashForWindows|clash-core-service' but mind the blast radius).
linux_app_register CFW \
  --exec='~/Documents/ClashForWindows/cfw' \
  --pkill='^/home/.+/Documents/ClashForWindows/cfw' \
  --wm-class='Clash for Windows'

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-13 12:54:33Z)**_

Two separate things — Bitwarden YES, Alacritty NO (footgun risk), and the Alacritty "new tab" question is a deliberate Alacritty design choice with two solutions.

**Why Bitwarden YES**: Snap-confined like Spotify, clean pattern, no risk.

**Why Alacritty NO**: `appquit Alacritty` matches *every* alacritty process — **including the one you're typing in**. Self-suicide risk; you'd lose your shell. For "quit the other Alacritty window", use the window's own ⌘W/⌃W instead.

**Alacritty + "new tab"**: Alacritty doesn't have tabs by design (upstream rejects it on principle — single-window terminal, multiplexer for tabs). Two paths to the same effect, and you already have one:

1. **tmux `prefix c`** (default `Ctrl+B c`) — new tmux window. The tmux status bar acts as your tab strip. This is what 90% of Alacritty users actually do (and what your tmux setup is built around).
2. **New Alacritty WINDOW** via `SpawnNewInstance` action — a separate process / taskbar entry. The Linux-terminal convention is `Ctrl+Shift+T`. Alacritty doesn't bind it by default; needs a config line.

Let me add Bitwarden, and add the `Ctrl+Shift+T` → new Alacritty window binding so you have the macOS-ish keystroke even if it's a window not a tab.

**About "new tab" in Alacritty** — to set expectations clearly:
- Alacritty has **no native tabs** by design (upstream explicitly rejects PRs for it — single-window terminal is the project's identity).
- `Ctrl+Shift+T` opens a **separate window**, not a tab. It'll show as a separate taskbar entry.
- For real "tab-strip-in-the-same-window" UX, you already have **tmux**. `prefix c` (Ctrl+B c by default) creates a new tmux window, and the tmux status bar gives you the tab strip. This is the workflow your whole tmux config is built around.
- If you want true GUI tabs, **Ghostty** (which this repo also configures) has them natively. But you'd be switching terminal, not adding tabs to Alacritty.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-13 13:05:56Z)**_

Correct observation — and that's not a bug, that's Alacritty's design speaking through your fingers. Let me clarify and offer a fix.

**Why both keys do the same thing:**

Alacritty has **exactly one** "make a new something" action: `SpawnNewInstance`. There is no `CreateNewTab` action because there are no tabs — upstream actively rejects PRs for it. So when I bound `T` and `N` to "the new thing," they both ended up at `SpawnNewInstance` → new window. Having two keys for the same thing is wasteful.

**What "real tab" looks like in this stack:**

The actual tab strip you're used to from Cmd+T = the tmux status bar at the bottom of your terminal. Each tmux window = one "tab." Your existing keystroke for it is `prefix c` (whatever your tmux prefix is + `c`). That creates a new tmux window inside the *same* Alacritty.

**Options for what to do with Ctrl+Shift+T:**

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-13 13:06:32Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**How should Ctrl+Shift+T behave on Linux Alacritty?**

Options:
- **Send tmux `prefix c` (new tmux window = real tab)** - Change Ctrl+Shift+T to send the tmux prefix + `c` byte sequence. Inside tmux this opens a new tmux window (the tab-strip equivalent). Outside tmux the keys reach the shell as `Ctrl+B c` which is mostly harmless (readline back-one-char + insert `c`). Recommended if you live in tmux 95%+ of the time. Keep Ctrl+Shift+N as new Alacritty WINDOW for the rare case you want a fresh desktop entry.
- **Drop Ctrl+Shift+T, keep only N for new window** - Remove the T binding entirely; Ctrl+Shift+N stays as the single new-window key. Most honest — no fake "tab" key when no tabs exist. You still get tabs via tmux `prefix c` (always-available, prefix-gated, no keypress collision).
- **Keep both as new-window (status quo)** - Leave the current bindings unchanged — both T and N open a new Alacritty window. Some users like having two muscle-memory paths to the same action (T from browser convention, N from app convention). Slight redundancy is the price.


**Answer:** Drop Ctrl+Shift+T, keep only N for new window
</details></tool-use>
